body.label: Scheme overview
body.text: The scheme provides targeted capital expenditure support of Rs.2,814 crore over five years (FY 2026-27 to 2030-31) to establish domestic processing facilities for critical minerals, specifically lithium and nickel.

body.label: Objectives
body.text: It aims to develop domestic processing capabilities to add value within India, reduce import dependence, and build resilient end-to-end value chains for critical minerals.

body.label: Subsidy details
body.text: A capital subsidy of 30% of eligible investment will be provided for setting up four processing plants: two lithium plants (minimum 30 kt capacity each) and two nickel plants (minimum 50 kt capacity each), with maximum support capped at Rs.500 crore per lithium beneficiary and Rs.900 crore per nickel beneficiary.

sections.heading: What is the Capex Support Scheme for Critical Mineral Processing?

body.label: Supply chain risks
body.text: Critical mineral processing is currently concentrated globally in few locations, exposing supply chains to geopolitical disruptions, price volatility, and supply restrictions, which threaten economic security and national security.

body.label: Import dependence
body.text: India is substantially dependent on imports for refined intermediates and high-purity materials like lithium, nickel, and cobalt due to limited domestic beneficiation and processing infrastructure.

body.label: Strategic sectors supported
body.text: Processed minerals will support electric mobility, Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), electronics, defence, and speciality steel sectors, aiding decarbonisation and industrial growth.

sections.heading: Why is this scheme important for India?

body.label: Selection process
body.text: Beneficiaries will be selected through a two-stage process: first, technical qualification assessment; second, financial bidding based on the least capital expenditure support sought.

body.label: Number of beneficiaries
body.text: For each mineral, two beneficiaries will be selected, making a total of four processing plants supported under the scheme.

body.label: Disbursement of incentives
body.text: Incentives will be disbursed in three tranches linked to achievement of specified project milestones.

sections.heading: How will beneficiaries be selected and supported?

body.label: Atmanirbhar Bharat
body.text: The scheme advances the Atmanirbhar Bharat objective by promoting resilient domestic processing infrastructure and reducing import dependence in critical mineral value chains.

body.label: Energy transition support
body.text: By supporting lithium and nickel processing, the scheme underpins sectors essential for energy transition such as electric vehicles and battery storage.

body.label: Complementary initiatives
body.text: It complements other government schemes like the Rs.14,500 crore Viability Gap Funding for grid-scale energy storage systems, which also aims to strengthen renewable energy integration and domestic manufacturing.

sections.heading: How does this scheme fit into India's broader energy and industrial strategy?

2026-11-04-pm-89d41d04af.anchor: Fiscal Federalism and Taxation Powers of States

back2basics.text: India’s Constitution divides taxation powers between the Union and States through three lists: Union List, State List, and Concurrent List. States have the power to tax sale or purchase of goods under Entry 54 of the State List. Additional sales tax or surcharge is a levy imposed by States as a percentage of the existing sales tax. The Goods and Services Tax (GST) is a unified tax regime that subsumes many indirect taxes, but constitutional interpretations of States’ taxation powers remain relevant for residual or specific levies.

2026-11-04-pm-89d41d04af.deck: The Supreme Court upheld a 1974 ruling affirming States' authority to impose additional sales tax as a percentage of existing sales tax, declaring a pending reference on the issue academic due to GST implementation. This ruling clarifies constitutional aspects of fiscal federalism relevant for taxation powers of States under the Constitution.

Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court ruling on States’ power to levy additional sales tax:

body.label: 1974 ruling upheld
body.text: The Supreme Court unanimously held that the 1974 Constitution Bench ruling in S. Kodar vs State of Kerala, which upheld States’ power to impose additional sales tax calculated as a percentage of existing sales tax, continues to hold the field.

body.label: Reference declared academic
body.text: A seven-judge Bench led by CJI Surya Kant declared the pending reference on this issue academic since the challenged statutory provisions were amended and GST now governs sales tax.

body.label: Nature of additional tax
body.text: The Court clarified that the additional tax or surcharge is an enhancement of the sales tax rate and not a tax on dealers’ income, thus falling within States’ legislative competence under Entry 54 of List II.

sections.heading: What did the Supreme Court rule about States’ power to levy additional sales tax?

body.label: Clarifies taxation powers
body.text: The ruling confirms that States have constitutional authority to impose additional sales tax or surcharge as part of their power to tax sale or purchase of goods.

body.label: Distinguishes tax types
body.text: It distinguishes additional sales tax from income tax, clarifying that States cannot be restricted from levying such surcharges under their legislative domain.

body.label: Impact of GST
body.text: While GST subsumes many indirect taxes, this ruling affirms that the earlier constitutional interpretation on States’ powers remains valid and relevant for any residual taxation powers.

sections.heading: Why does this ruling matter for the Constitution and federalism?

body.label: Orissa Sales Tax Act challenge
body.text: The case arose from a challenge to Section 5A of the Orissa Sales Tax Act, which imposed additional tax rates of 10% or 15% on dealers based on turnover thresholds.

body.label: Constitutional dispute
body.text: The question was whether the State legislature had competence under Entry 54 of List II to impose this levy or whether it was effectively an income tax, which only Parliament can impose under Entry 82 of List I.

body.label: Earlier Supreme Court decisions
body.text: The controversy stemmed from differing interpretations, but the 1974 five-judge Bench ruling had upheld additional sales tax as a valid enhancement of sales tax.

sections.heading: What was the background of the case and the legal question involved?

back2basics.text: An official statistical system collects, processes, and disseminates data to inform government policy and public knowledge. body.label: Key objectives
body.text: It aims to enhance timeliness, data granularity, interoperability, and AI readiness of datasets, enabling flexible resource allocation for surveys, research, digital transformation, and national data governance.

body.label: Scope
body.text: The scheme covers all statistical and data management activities of the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) to upgrade the official statistical system.

sections.heading: What is the VISTAR scheme and its objectives?

body.label: Component 1: Statistical Operations
body.text: MoSPI will conduct 59 surveys during the 16th Finance Commission cycle, up from 43 previously, filling critical data gaps and improving policy decisions.

body.label: Component 2: Support for Statistical Strengthening
body.text: Funds will be provided to States and UTs under a redesigned framework (SSS 2.0) to build capacity for producing high-quality, granular data at district and city levels and embed data use in local policymaking.

body.label: Component 3: Economic Census
body.text: The 8th Economic Census will collect detailed data on non-farm establishments and workers up to Gram Panchayat and Ward levels, assessing the unorganized sector and forming the baseline for the National Statistical Business Register.

sections.heading: What are the main components of the VISTAR scheme?

body.label: Digital transformation
body.text: MoSPI will digitize statistical processes end-to-end and integrate Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for data processing, validation, and analysis.

body.label: New metrics and data harmonisation
body.text: New indices like the Headline Index of Services Production and Index of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises will be introduced, supported by data cataloguing, machine readability, interoperability, and privacy by design.

body.label: Alternate data sources
body.text: The scheme will mainstream alternative data sources such as mobile phone, scanner, and e-commerce data to complement traditional surveys, reduce respondent burden, and fill data gaps.

body.label: Capacity building
body.text: Opportunities for youth and researchers will be enhanced through internships and research proposals from academic institutions.

sections.heading: How will VISTAR improve data quality and usage?

body.label: Evidence-based policymaking
body.text: Improved and timely data will enable targeted policy interventions and better decision-making at national and sub-national levels.

body.label: Unorganized sector assessment
body.text: Economic Census data will help estimate the contribution of the unorganized sector to GDP, aiding planners and policymakers.

body.label: State-level empowerment
body.text: By strengthening statistical capabilities at the state and district levels, VISTAR supports localized policymaking and indigenous data processing.

back2basics.text: The Liquidity Adjustment Facility is a monetary policy tool used by RBI to manage liquidity in the banking system. It involves repo operations, where RBI lends money to banks, and reverse repo operations, where RBI borrows money from banks. The variable rate reverse repo auction allows RBI to absorb excess liquidity by borrowing funds overnight at variable interest rates, helping to regulate short-term interest rates and maintain monetary stability.

body.label: Definition
body.text: The Overnight Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auction is a monetary policy tool used by RBI under the Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) to absorb excess liquidity from the banking system by borrowing funds overnight at variable rates.

body.label: Purpose
body.text: It helps RBI manage short-term liquidity conditions and influence overnight interest rates, ensuring they remain within the policy corridor.

body.label: Recent auction details
body.text: On November 3, 2026, RBI conducted a VRRR auction with a notified amount of ₹50,000 crore for a one-day tenor, with the auction window from 10:45 AM to 11:15 AM and settlement on November 4, 2026.

sections.heading: What is the Overnight Variable Rate Reverse Repo auction?

body.label: Liquidity absorption
body.text: RBI's operations on November 2 and 3, 2026, show net liquidity absorption of ₹1,87,840 crore and ₹1,92,952 crore respectively, indicating RBI is actively managing surplus liquidity in the banking system.

body.label: Interest rates in money markets
body.text: Weighted average rates in overnight segments ranged between 4.80% and 5.95% on November 2 and between 0.01% and 5.90% on November 3, reflecting the influence of RBI’s liquidity operations.

body.label: Use of multiple instruments
body.text: RBI uses various instruments like repo, reverse repo, Marginal Standing Facility (MSF), and Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) to fine-tune liquidity and maintain monetary stability.

sections.heading: How do RBI's money market operations reflect liquidity management?

body.label: Understanding monetary policy tools
body.text: VRRR auctions and liquidity operations are key components of RBI’s monetary policy toolkit, which aspirants must understand for questions on resource mobilisation, growth, and development.

body.label: Link to interest rates and inflation
body.text: These operations influence short-term interest rates, which affect credit availability, inflation, and overall economic stability, topics relevant for both prelims and mains.

body.label: Current affairs relevance
body.text: Recent RBI auctions exemplify real-time monetary policy actions, useful for illustrating answers on financial market regulation and monetary management.
